Power has become a harder constraint on AI than chips.

A 1 GW data center waiting on power loses about $8 million a day to chip depreciation alone. That cost is pushing developers to pay up for fuel cells, build gas plants on site and run generators made from retired jet engines.

Most of those are stopgaps until a large gas turbine comes free. GE Vernova’s backlog has reached about six years of output. The wait is long enough that SpaceX plans to cast its own turbine blades.

On-site gas and fuel cells fill the gap for the next few years. The largest tech companies are also paying up for clean power to take over after that. Google agreed in October to pay more than double the cost of a new gas plant for extra output from existing nuclear reactors.

Some are betting even further out on advanced reactors, next-generation geothermal and fusion power that has never reached the grid.

The demand behind those bets is still climbing. Data centers used under 5% of U.S. electricity in 2024. Forecasts for 2030 now run as high as 17% and keep getting revised up.

Anyone who can deliver power faster than the grid will be able to charge for it.

re: the “communist/socialist” boogeyman in America

what’s interesting is you see a lot of Republican candidates pushing this messaging as a way to discredit Democratic challengers in races across the country (especially at the national level)

but it’s not really detracting from their appeal anymore. why?

the terms communism, socialism, etc. had much greater relevance to people in prior decades due to the Soviet threat. everyone associated communism with the USSR. and there was very little integration and trade between the US and USSR

but ofc, the USSR no longer exists. so what about China? aren’t they communist?

sort of, but to people sitting in the US, China actually comes across as hyper-capitalist (albeit authoritarian), especially on the global stage. i.e., people buy a ton of Chinese products (knowingly and unknowingly) and know that they are now maybe the greatest physically productive nation on the planet today

so the terms “communist” and “socialist” don’t have the same negative connotation they once had. we’re a full generation past the collapse of the USSR. and the one great power which is called “communist” seems to not be collapsing under its own weight

combine this with the specter of AI-related job losses and you can see why these ideologies are becoming more appealing to more people, especially when people can see that the government is increasingly corrupt and their cost of living is getting much worse relative to their wages

i don’t think socialism as it’s conceived of by organizations such as the DSA is the answer at all, but you’d have to be blind not to see that we need revisions to our economic model if it cannot sustain a thriving middle class of workers (especially in the face of greater destruction of that middle class through AI). even Elon seems to acknowledge this by talking about “universal high income”

the longer it takes us to start having these discussions, the more calamitous it will be once the boiling point is reached

anyway, don’t shoot the messenger…

• The pool then forwarded 195,460 ETH to a fresh, unlabeled EOA
• That EOA has only one transaction and currently holds the 195,460 ETH.

I think we can go ahead and assume DPRK.
